question: What is the primary goal of preventive nursing in endocrine care?

options.C: Stopping disease onset and managing complications

explanation: Preventive nursing aims to stop diseases before they start and effectively manage existing conditions to prevent severe outcomes. [learn more](GNS222_U2_T17#GNS222_U2_T17_h1)

question: Why are nurses considered frontline workers in metabolic disease prevention?

options.A: They possess sole legal authority to diagnose endocrine disorders
options.B: They interact continuously with communities and assess individual risk factors
options.C: They are responsible for manufacturing essential metabolic medications
options.D: They manage hospital budgets for diagnostic equipment purchases

explanation: Nurses have direct, ongoing contact with patients, making them ideally positioned to spot early risk factors and educate communities. [learn more](GNS222_U2_T17#GNS222_U2_T17_h1)

question: A key strategy in primary prevention of type 2 diabetes is...

options.A: promoting regular physical activity and healthy diets
options.B: surgically reducing the size of the pancreas
options.C: initiating lifelong daily insulin injections immediately
options.D: performing monthly diagnostic blood glucose curves

explanation: Primary prevention focuses on lifestyle changes like diet and exercise to stop the disease from developing. [learn more](GNS222_U2_T17#GNS222_U2_T17_h2)

question: What advice should a nurse give a patient to improve insulin sensitivity?

options.A: Eliminate all forms of water intake after evening meals
options.B: Engage in regular moderate aerobic exercise each week
options.C: Avoid routine medical checkups if feeling completely healthy
options.D: Increase consumption of refined sugar for quick energy

explanation: Physical activity helps skeletal muscles take up glucose without needing as much insulin, improving overall sensitivity. [learn more](GNS222_U2_T17#GNS222_U2_T17_h2)

question: What is the main objective of secondary prevention in endocrine health?

options.A: Providing emergency care for diabetic ketoacidosis
options.C: Early detection of disease in asymptomatic individuals
options.D: Reversing complete destruction of pancreatic tissue

explanation: Secondary prevention relies on screening tests to catch metabolic issues before symptoms or complications manifest. [learn more](GNS222_U2_T17#GNS222_U2_T17_h3)

question: Why is routine blood pressure screening vital for metabolic syndrome prevention?

options.A: Blood pressure readings provide an exact measurement of blood sugar
options.B: Cuff pressure stimulates the thyroid gland to release excess hormones
options.C: Hypertension often coexists silently with insulin resistance and vascular damage
options.D: High blood pressure directly destroys insulin-producing beta cells

explanation: Metabolic syndrome clusters conditions like hypertension and high blood sugar, which silently damage the cardiovascular system together. [learn more](GNS222_U2_T17#GNS222_U2_T17_h3)

question: Tertiary prevention in metabolic care is best defined as...

options.A: screening healthy populations for elevated blood glucose
options.B: administering vaccines to prevent viral endocrine destruction
options.C: managing established disease to prevent further complications
options.D: teaching nutrition classes to elementary school children

explanation: Tertiary prevention focuses on treatment, rehabilitation, and complication management for patients who already have the disease. [learn more](GNS222_U2_T17#GNS222_U2_T17_h4)

question: A patient with long-standing diabetes presents with a foot ulcer. What level of prevention is required?
explanation: Treating an existing complication like a foot ulcer falls squarely under tertiary prevention to limit further disability. [learn more](GNS222_U2_T17#GNS222_U2_T17_h4)

question: Why is self-management empowerment essential for patients with endocrine disorders?

options.A: Patients prefer diagnosing their own laboratory results independently
options.B: Medical treatments only work if administered without nurse supervision
options.C: Daily disease control relies mostly on the patient's routine choices
options.D: Hospitals lack the capacity to provide any outpatient follow-up

explanation: Endocrine disorders require round-the-clock self-care, making patient empowerment vital for day-to-day management success. [learn more](GNS222_U2_T17#GNS222_U2_T17_h5)

question: What is a primary goal of culturally sensitive dietary education for diabetic patients?

options.A: Eliminating all cultural practices related to family meal times
options.B: Importing expensive foreign foods for proper metabolic control
options.C: Forbidding the consumption of any traditional carbohydrate staples
options.D: Using locally available foods to make healthy eating sustainable

explanation: Education works best when it incorporates affordable and familiar local food options that patients can realistically maintain. [learn more](GNS222_U2_T17#GNS222_U2_T17_h5)

question: How does multidisciplinary collaboration improve outcomes in endocrine nursing?

options.A: It reduces the total number of diagnostic tests a patient must undergo
options.B: It combines diverse professional expertise to provide comprehensive patient care
options.C: It allows nurses to bypass physicians and prescribe medications directly
options.D: It eliminates the need for any direct patient involvement in care

explanation: Complex metabolic diseases require insights from various specialists, working together to address all facets of the patient's health. [learn more](GNS222_U2_T17#GNS222_U2_T17_h6)

question: A nurse notices a diabetic patient struggling with diet adherence. Who should the nurse involve in the care team?
explanation: Dietitians specialize in creating practical meal plans that match metabolic needs, making them the ideal team member to consult. [learn more](GNS222_U2_T17#GNS222_U2_T17_h6)
